text:
maya: Quick sync on Sparrow-9p5 bring-up. Ran fp16 / int8 / int6 on the longform summarization slice (news + policy docs). High-level: int6 cuts token cost ~2.4x vs fp16, latency win ~20%, but we see quality drops concentrated on long-context sections (>=1200 tokens): ROUGE-L down ~6 pts, hallucination rate up ~3.5% on citation sections. gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/sparrow-9p5-quant-summary :thumbsup:

zach: ack. can you paste the small slice of the failure cases? curious if it's priming or context-window truncation noise.

maya: sure, two short examples inline.
maya: "Input: 3500-token policy doc with multiple nested lists. Expected: concise enumerated summary with citations."
maya: "fp16: correct numbered list, citations preserved. int6: merges bullets, invents a citation id 'Section 4.1' that doesn't exist. int8: mostly OK but weaker on ordering."

linh: hmm. that sounds like quant-induced attention degradation for long KV cache chains. we've seen similar with other 9B-ish archs where int6 math stability hurts cross-sentence coreference.

maya: agree. I ran a quick attention-variance probe and int6 shows higher variance at step > 1024. eva-bot: automated eval summary -> {\"slice\": \"longform_news_policy\", \"fp16_ROUGE-L\": \"42.1\", \"int8_ROUGE-L\": \"40.4\", \"int6_ROUGE-L\": \"36.0\", \"hallucination_pct_fp16\": \"1.1\", \"hallucination_pct_int6\": \"4.6\"}.

amy_pm: product ask: we need a recommendation for GTN and a short stoplight for product owners (enable/disable, when to route to safer model). Can we propose guardrails?

zach: proposal: hybrid routing based on input length and signal classifier (citation_density + doc_type). Quick rules: if tokens > 1200 OR citation_density > 0.2 -> route to fp16 variant. Else default int6. Add fallback threshold: if output_confidence < 0.65 -> re-run on fp16.

maya: drafted routing config snippet: ```json
{
  "routes": [
    {"name": "longform_fp16", "condition": "tokens>1200 or citation_density>0.2", "model": "sparrow-9p5-fp16"},
    {"name": "short_int6", "condition": "else", "model": "sparrow-9p5-int6"}
  ],
  "fallbacks": {"low_confidence": {"threshold": 0.65, "action": "reroute to sparrow-9p5-fp16"}}
}
```

linh: +1. Also recommend we enable a cheap shallow QA check for factual anchors: extract top-3 claims and run a small retriever+verify; if mismatch rate > 0.15 reroute. That will reduce false positives from the rerun policy.

amy_pm: for GTN guidance: propose "Enable int6 for chat+short docs; require fp16 for long-form and docs with citations. Add the fallback policy above. Rollout: canary to 10% traffic for 48h, monitor ROUGE-L, hallucination and error rate. If hallucination delta > 2% abort."

zach: ops note: int6 infra footprint is nice but we'll need auto-burst to fp16 for reruns. cost calc: with expected 30% of traffic routed to fp16 due to long docs + reruns, net unit cost ~1.35x vs pure int6 but still ~0.55x vs fp16-only.

maya: action items: 1) prod enable routing flags + classifier (linh) 2) add retriever-check hook (zach) 3) GTN brief + stoplight + canary plan (amy). I'll post the full bench artifacts in the benchboard.

eva-bot: bench artifacts uploaded -> https://internal.redwood/bench/sparrow-9p5/1718501234 : results csv + failcases.txt

amy_pm: thanks. i'll draft the GTN note and include the stoplight + rollback thresholds. :rocket:

zach: one more: let's add a small A/B that compares int8 vs int6 default for chat (same routing) — int8 might be a middle ground and avoid some longform regressions while keeping cost ~1.6x fp16. anyone opposed?

maya: sounds good. let's run a 2-week micro-canary on chat traffic.

linh: i'll prepare the classifier label set and send to the labeling queue.

maya: cool. wrapping up here — will follow up with a short doc summarizing numbers and the exact config to land in the router.
